Description of Expected Content: Detailed comments on how you have derived the cost of the Retrofit Straegy. Include sources for each major item, per sq ft rate breakdowns.  Include sentence on overall confidence.
Instructions for GPT: Provide a deep analysis and synthesis of all costs. Structure as: statement on how you have derived the cost of the Retrofit Strategy, high level breakdown clustered by intervention theme (fabric, MEP, etc), source attribution, comparison to market benchmarks, where works are more or less involved than benchmarks. End with sentence on overall confidence.
Examples: Total retrofit cost £3.2m / £87 per sq ft. Plant-room replacement (ASHP + calorifiers + reconfigured primary circuits) at £1.1m is 34% of total, benchmarked against RICS/BCIS median for 2024 commercial retrofit. Floor MEP refurbishment at £0.62m (19% of total) aligns with JLL London retrofit indices Q1 2025. Enhanced glazing at £0.38m sits at the upper end of BCIS data because the existing 2014 curtain wall system is obsolete and requires full re-glazing rather than film retrofit — a material cost premium over typical refurb programmes. 200 kWp PV at £240k is market-median for 2025 UK commercial solar. Professional fees at 15% (£0.42m) reflect the complexity of phased delivery around the WPP tenant. Overall confidence ±15%; main cost risk is fabric discovery during strip-out, particularly if the roof membrane proves to need replacement concurrent with the PV installation.

Description of Expected Content: Investment-relevant synthesis of IMD deprivation data across all domains, identifying area trajectory, hidden risks, and explicit investment implications
Dependencies: lsoa_code, imd_barriers_decile, imd_crime_decile, imd_decile, imd_education_decile, imd_employment_decile, imd_health_decile, imd_idaci_decile, imd_idaopi_decile, imd_income_decile, imd_living_env_decile, imd_population_total, imd_rank, imd_score
Instructions for GPT: Using the raw IMD data in context above, synthesise into an investment-relevant narrative. Structure as: (1) DEPRIVATION PROFILE - state overall decile and national rank context (e.g., 'Decile 7 places this LSOA in the least deprived 40% nationally'); (2) DOMAIN TENSIONS - identify any decile spreads >3 between domains as these signal gentrification pressure, hidden risk, or market dislocation (e.g., high income decile but low living environment suggests underinvestment in housing stock); (3) RESILIENCE INDICATORS - employment, education, and health deciles are leading indicators of area trajectory - state whether these suggest improving, stable, or declining fundamentals; (4) INVESTMENT IMPLICATIONS - state clearly whether IMD profile supports or challenges the investment thesis, citing specific domain evidence. Be direct. No hedging. If the data is unfavourable for investment, say so explicitly. Cross-reference with IDACI/IDAOPI to flag demographic-specific risks.
Notes: Domain tensions are key - uniform deciles across domains suggest stable areas; high variance suggests areas in transition (opportunity or risk). Employment + Education trending high = gentrification tailwind. Crime decile <4 with Income decile >6 = investor caution.
Examples: This LSOA sits in Decile 6 (rank 15,420 of 32,844), placing it in the least deprived 40% nationally. However, significant domain tension exists: Income (Decile 7) and Employment (Decile 8) contrast sharply with Living Environment (Decile 3) and Barriers to Housing (Decile 4). This 4-5 point spread signals an area where economic fundamentals outpace physical infrastructure—a classic gentrification signature. Resilience indicators are strong: Education (Decile 7) and Health (Decile 6) suggest stable, upwardly-mobile demographics. IDACI (Decile 8) confirms low child poverty, reinforcing family-friendly positioning. Investment implication: IMD profile supports the thesis. The infrastructure lag (living environment, housing barriers) represents exactly the value-add opportunity a retrofit strategy can capture. Crime Decile 7 removes security discount concerns. Proceed with confidence.

(2) Selective glazing replacement where individual curtain-wall units are approaching end-of-life, addressing approximately 12% of fabric-related energy loss without triggering full fabric re-envelope — a lower-cost targeted intervention.
